newsitem.title: USA: Maine PUC staff opposes Bangor Hydro rate request.
newsitem.headline: Maine PUC staff opposes Bangor Hydro rate request.

text.p: The Maine Public Utilities Commission's advocacy staff has recommended regulators turn down Bangor Hydro's $10 million emergency rate hike.
The staff said the utility's financial situation is "certainly serious," but that it has not explored all its options or demonstrated the need for the rate hike at this time.

"It is not clear based on the information provided, even if the company's request was fully granted, that its current difficulties with its lenders would be resolved," the staff said in writen comments on the request.

Bangor Hydro filed a request for an emergency rate hike in April, citing financial problems caused largely by the extended shudown of the Maine Yankee nuclear plant. The utility owns 7 percent of Maine Yankee.

"While the company is technically in default on certain financial performance convenants contained in its loan agreements, the company has not demonstrated that sufficiently adverse consequences will result from this default or that the emergency rate relief requested, if granted, could present any such adverse results," the PUC staff wrote.

The PUC is taking testimony on the rate request and is expected to issue its ruling in early July. By filing the request on an emergency basis, Bangor Hydro shortened the amount of time regulators have to consider the request.

The Maine Yankee nuclear plant has been shutdown since Dec. 6, for safety-related repairs, refueling and a steam generator inspection and is not expected to restart until later summer at the earliest.
